CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory symptoms starting last night.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient began feeling ill around supper time last night with onset of runny nose and nasal congestion. Nasal mucus is clear. Associated symptoms include non-barky cough, ear pulling, and nasal rubbing. Rectal temperature taken by guardian measured 100.3°F this morning. Appetite was good last night but decreased this morning - consumed approximately 7 ounces from bottle, barely finished second bottle, and refused cereal. Patient is energetic but irritable and resisting sleep. Guardian noted generalized sweating earlier this morning. Recent exposures include sick older sister and nephew with sinus infection. Home treatments attempted include saline nasal mist, acetaminophen given early this morning, baby Vick's applied to feet last night, and humidifier. Guardian also reports worsening cradle cap, currently treating with cradle cap brush and Aveeno shampoo.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Respiratory: Runny nose with clear mucus, nasal congestion, non-barky cough, nasal rubbing.
Ears: Ear pulling.
Fever: Rectal temperature 100.3°F.
Appetite: Good last night, decreased this morning.
Behavior: Irritable, energetic but fighting sleep.
Systemic: Generalized sweating noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Cradle cap.

MEDICATIONS
Saline nasal mist, acetaminophen, baby Vick's.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Cooperative and interactive.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, breathing well.
Ears: Normal.

RESULTS
Rectal temperature: 100.3°F.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Viral upper respiratory infection/sinusitis - Early viral illness; no antibiotics indicated at this time, though may progress to bacterial infection if left untreated. Monitor closely.

2. Cradle cap - Worsening.

Plan:
- Continue supportive care with fluids and rest.
- Monitor closely for development of barking cough. If barky cough develops, administer half teaspoon of medication (same as sister's) once daily for 5 days.
- Prescription provided for croup medication.
- For non-barky cough: Zarbee's using under 1 year pediatric dosing.
- For nasal congestion: Continue saline mist; Zarbee's (under 1 year dosing).
- Counseled against honey due to botulism risk; agave recommended as alternative.
- For cradle cap: Apply Head & Shoulders, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral AD (regular strength) twice weekly. Continue soft brush and baby oil to remove scales. Avoid eye contact during rinsing. Expected improvement within 6 weeks.
- Follow-up appointment in 1 week.
- Contact office if symptoms worsen.
